newsitem.title: COTE D'IVOIRE: Ivorian rains below average but no cocoa damage.
newsitem.headline: Ivorian rains below average but no cocoa damage.

text.p: Ivory Coast's dry season in July favoured drying of mid-crop cocoa (May-Sept) but will not damage pod growth for 1997/98 (Oct-April), analysts said on Wednesday.
July rains would be below average after a sharp drop-off from high wet season totals in May and June, but overall conditions were still favourable for development of pod fruits.

"A July deficit is on the cards but it is not necessarily a problem," one said. "We had the same situation in 1994 when rains for the month averaged 60 mm but despite all the fears there was no real damage."
Blanket cloud cover, cool air temperatures and good soil moisture retention prevailing in July had so far countered potential threats to developing cocoa, he added.
Official national weather data for the second 10 days of July show rains averaged 14.8 mm at 10 monitored stations, against 16.7 mm in the previous 10 days.
Rainfall was about 10 times lighter than in the same period in June, which turned out to be an abnormally wet month ahead of the July-August dry season.
Regional buyers have reported some rains but a front that was shifting north meant dry weather was set to continue into August. Heavier rains usually arrive in September, analysts say.
Plantations visited by Reuters in July showed no signs of water shortage although showers were light and brief.
French-Swiss chocolate-maker Barry Callebaut, which has two factories in Ivory Coast, has predicted a 1997/98 crop of 1.1 million tonnes.
London broker GNI said in a recent report the crop could top 1.2 million tonnes -- the size of the 1995/96 record harvest -- if weather remained favourable.
Most crop analysts issue preliminary forecasts in August when the effects of dry season weather are more clear.

The latest weather data, from Ivory Coast's national weather station, showed the following rainfall (mm) for the second 10 days of July in key growing areas plus the commercial capital Abidjan (previous 10 days in brackets).

Daloa 86.5 (10.7), Gagnoa 4.4 (10.5), San Pedro 0 (1.8), Tabou 33.0 (2.8), Man 14.4 (80.6), Dimbokro 6.6 (29.2), Yamoussoukro 0.6 (25.6), Abidjan 0 (0.1), Sassandra 0 (2.7), Adiake 2.9 (5.9). -- Abidjan newsroom + 225 21 90 90
